hpi:
{{patient_name}} is a young woman presenting to the ED with heavy menstrual bleeding. Classic vWD at menarche: anemia on CBC with normal platelets; PT normal, mildly elevated PTT, normal fibrinogen; decreased ristocetin-induced platelet aggregation.

Workup: CBC/hemoglobin; PT/PTT; platelet aggregation; TSH (rule out hypothyroid menorrhagia); pelvic/genital exam; vWF activity or hematology consult (confirmatory labs take 3 days).

Acute treatment: IV fluids for hypovolemia (Hgb ~10 — not transfusion threshold); DDAVP and tranexamic acid together for mucosal bleeding; iron for anemia. Long-term: hormonal therapy or OB/GYN consult; avoid NSAIDs and contact sports until diagnosis confirmed.

patient_voice.chief_complaint: My periods are extremely heavy — I'm soaking through pads every hour
patient_voice.history: This started around when my periods began. I've been tired and bruise easily. My gums bleed when I brush.
patient_voice.pain: Cramping with the heavy flow — I'm also dizzy when I stand up

case_summary:
Differential: Von Willebrand disease (vWD), Thrombocytopenia, Hemophilia A, Platelet Abnormalities (Glanzmann thrombasthenia), Vasculopathies, Connective Tissue Diseases, Collagen Disorders, hypothyroidism.

The first step is to assess anemia and platelet count by getting a CBC. This shows anemia but normal platelets. Then order PT/PTT, revealing normal PT, mildly elevated PTT, and normal fibrinogen, pointing toward vWD. This is a classic presentation for vWD diagnosis in females around menarche due to heavy periods. Once suspected, order vWF assays showing decreased ristocetin-induced platelet aggregation at 1.0 mg/mL, suggestive of type 1 vWD. Confirmatory vWF activity takes 3 days, so the case ends before results, but initial findings allow empirical treatment.

Start IV fluids for hypovolemia. Give DDAVP (desmopressin) concurrently with tranexamic acid for acute bleeding control. DDAVP boosts endogenous vWF/Factor VIII. Tranexamic acid is an adjunct for mucosal bleeding — start with DDAVP, not after failure.

Preventive care: oral contraceptives or OB/GYN consult; iron for anemia; counsel to avoid NSAIDs and contact sports.
